text.p: These are the leading stories in Malawian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Malawi's 177-seat parliament has seven vacant seats to be competed for in by-elections and has lost, through death, up to 12 members since the transition to multi-party politics two years ago.

- Natural Resources Minister Melvin Moyo is at the centre of a wrangle with his ministry's officials for allegedly forcing them to hire him a more comfortable car after refusing to use a Toyota Venture allocated to him. A ministry official said Moyo had by December 5 accumulated K89,980 ($5,998) debt with a hiring firm and was continuing to use a hired Toyota Prado.

- A proposed visit to South Africa by President Bakili Muluzi last Wednesday was cancelled allegedly because of revelations in parliament that migrant labour funds in South Africa were mismanaged by some government officials. Presidential press officer Alaudin Osman said, however, President Muluzi, invited by South African President Nelson Mandela to attend an SADC function, had cancelled the trip for technical reason.

- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) on Saturday challenged chiefs in Lilongwe, central Malawi, to go back to the electorate to consult them on whether to continue a boycott of parliament. Chiefs in Lilongwe asked their members of parliament, through the district commissioner, to abandon the boycot and return to parliament.

- University students will on Thursday march to the National Assembly where parliament is meeting without the opposition, to petition speaker Rodwell Munyenyembe for a resumption of classes. University students were sent home in July after lecturers boycotted classes and refused to administer final year examinations.

- Functionaries of the ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) top the list of offenders in electoral frauds in by-elections, said a police report last week. In one by-election, out of 13 alleged offences reported to police, 11 were committed by UDF functionaries, the report said.
